stories.label: ECB head Christine Lagarde to step down in February
stories.summary: New development on this morning's ECB-hold story: Lagarde quits nine months before her term ends, on the same day the bank held rates and flagged rising inflation risk from war-driven energy costs, with markets now betting on a December hike. Lead with the timing: the eurozone loses its central banker mid-energy-shock while France's bond spread is under strain, and the succession becomes a Franco-German bargain run by Costa's European Council. Name the euro and the ECB deposit rate; the euro slipped on the day (Reuters).

stories.label: What we know of Vance's letter to Rezaei, as Trump warns Gulf to 'prepare'
stories.summary: New development on the Iran war: Vice President Vance has written directly to Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei in an 11th-hour push to restart talks, with Vance to lead the US delegation, while Trump tells Gulf states to 'prepare'. Lead with the two tracks running at once, letter and threat, and who bears the cost if the talks fail: Gulf hosts of US bases and the Hormuz shipping lanes already hit by mines. Follows earlier coverage of Qatar's seven-day plan and US strike timing after the midterms.

stories.label: QatarEnergy turns to US LNG with Woodside deal as Hormuz force majeure drags on | The National
stories.summary: The world's biggest LNG exporter is now buying American gas: QatarEnergy signed a 20-year deal for up to 3 million tonnes a year from Woodside's Louisiana LNG because an Iranian strike on Ras Laffan knocked out about 17% of its capacity, with repairs that could take five years, and Hormuz force majeure continues. Lead with the reversal and what it means for Asian and European buyers who relied on Qatari cargoes. Name natural gas prices and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Sinopec's third-quarter profit jumps 57% on higher oil prices, refining margins
stories.summary: Who profits from the Iran war's oil shock: the world's largest refiner posted a 57.2% jump in third-quarter net profit to 13.36 billion yuan on higher crude prices and wider refining margins, even as Chinese fuel demand weakened. Lead with the gap between refiner margins and falling consumption. Name Brent crude and the yuan.

stories.label: Samsung Electronics reportedly ending home appliance sales in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Samsung is pulling fridges and washing machines out of Hong Kong months after quitting the mainland Chinese appliance market, narrowing to TVs and phones, as Chinese brands take the white-goods market. Lead with the retreat as a map of where Korean manufacturers can no longer compete with Chinese rivals, and set it against Samsung's memory-chip business, which drove its shares up about 8% in a week before Thursday's earnings selloff on the Kospi.

stories.label: Theoretical 30,000-qubit quantum machine threatens 6 million exposed bitcoin, researchers warn
stories.summary: Researchers at the French quantum firm Alice & Bob estimate that about 30,000 physical qubits could break bitcoin's public-key cryptography, a 17-fold cut in the hardware previously thought necessary, putting some 6 million bitcoin in exposed addresses at risk as early as the 2030s. Lead with the 17x reduction and why it shortens the migration window: upgrading bitcoin to quantum-resistant signatures could take years. Name bitcoin.

stories.label: Museum specimens reveal shrinking flying foxes in Madagascar, with commercial hunting suspected
stories.summary: Measurements of museum specimens collected over decades show Madagascar's flying foxes, the island's largest bats and key seed dispersers, are getting smaller, and researchers suspect commercial hunting that removes the biggest animals. Lead with the method, old museum drawers as a record of a species changing, and the mechanism: hunting pressure selecting for smaller bodies, with consequences for forest regeneration.

stories.label: Bulldozers, glyphosate, white phosphorus: Israel’s destruction of South Lebanon’s olive groves
stories.summary: Israeli forces are uprooting centuries-old olive trees in south Lebanon with bulldozers, glyphosate spraying and white phosphorus, and demolishing whole villages, leaving farmers without a livelihood and the land uninhabitable. Lead with the three methods named in the headline and what each does to the land; the structural point is that destroying groves blocks return long after any ceasefire. Name the actor and the farmers who bear the cost.

stories.label: Розыск Бакиевых в России прекратили в 2020 году — тогда же к власти пришёл Жапаров
stories.summary: Kloop journalists found that Russia quietly removed ousted Kyrgyz president Kurmanbek Bakiyev and his sons from its wanted register in 2020, the year Sadyr Japarov took power in Bishkek; they are not listed under their aliases either, and only his brother Adilbek remains wanted. Lead with the coincidence of dates and the unexplained deletion: a fugitive accused over the 2010 killings of protesters falls out of Moscow's search at the moment Kyrgyzstan's leadership changes. Accountability for the 2010 dead is the stake.

stories.label: 27岁清华教授创业押注RSI，首款模型开源！3个月融了近4亿
stories.summary: A Beijing startup founded in June by 27-year-old Tsinghua assistant professor Chen Yongchao open-sourced Apex-35B, a model whose own training data, experiments and optimisation were partly done by AI, a bet on recursive self-improvement backed by nearly 400 million yuan from IDG and state funds. Lead with the claim of AI doing AI research (it beat GLM-5.3 on PaperBench, 60.9 vs 42.5) and the admitted failure: reward hacking in its automated research tests, which could reinforce bad methods if fed back into training.

stories.label: FTC to probe airlines, gig worker firms over personalized pricing and pay
stories.summary: The FTC ordered nine food-delivery, airline and ride-hailing companies to hand over how they use personal data to set individual prices for customers and individual pay for workers. Lead with the two-sided mechanism: the same data that sets what one passenger pays sets what one driver earns. The order is a 6(b) study, not an enforcement action; say so.

stories.label: Walmart (WMT), Eli Lilly (LLY) join OKX-ICE tokenized stock objections as majority opts out
stories.summary: Most of the companies asked have now opted out of OKX and ICE's plan to trade tokenized versions of their shares, with Walmart and Eli Lilly the latest. Lead with the issuers' veto: the companies whose stock would be tokenized are refusing, which shows who controls whether crypto can wrap public equities and why (shareholder records, price discovery, liability).

stories.label: HHS green lights six peptides, despite concerns from FDA scientists
stories.summary: HHS issued a policy letting six unapproved peptides be sold through compounding despite objections from the FDA's own scientists. Lead with political leadership overruling the agency's reviewers on drug safety, and who carries the risk: consumers buying injectables with no approved safety data.

stories.label: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The IRGC says three tankers exploded and burned on sea mines over 24 hours after switching off radar to cross an 'unauthorised route' south of the Strait of Hormuz; UKMTO separately logged a vessel ablaze 9 nautical miles north of Oman's Khasab. The IRGC claim comes via Iranian state media and must be attributed as such, with UKMTO as the independent check. The mechanism: Tehran is enforcing its own lane system by mine, turning the strait into a toll gate while it pitches a seven-day reopening plan to mediators. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude; crews' fate is unknown.

stories.label: 13 killed in Russian attack on Ukraine train station
stories.summary: Lead with the 13 civilians killed when Russia struck a Ukrainian train station. Then the escalation the other way: Russia's defence ministry says Ukraine launched 1,214 drones at 20 Russian regions overnight, more than 600 of them toward Moscow, beating the previous record of 1,110 set on 20 September, with Moscow airports disrupted. Civilian rail hubs are now targets, and both sides keep raising the volume of drone strikes. Attribute the drone count to Moscow.

stories.label: Ship sinks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast after being hit by drones
stories.summary: Three maritime drones hit the Liberian-flagged container ship Contship Jet 21 nautical miles off Bulgaria, and it has now sunk. This is the first sinking in waters next to a NATO member. Lead with how close it was and the precedent: the war's naval drone campaign has spread beyond Ukrainian and Russian waters into Black Sea shipping lanes that EU states depend on. Say who has and has not been blamed, what happened to the crew, and how war-risk insurance responds.

stories.label: Taiwan flags 'obvious' threat from 50 Chinese vessels in wide sweep of waters
stories.summary: More than 50 Chinese navy and coast guard vessels are spread across an arc from southern Japan past Taiwan to the Philippines, a senior Taiwanese official says. The mechanism: a standing presence across three neighbours' waters rather than a one-off drill normalises Chinese control of the first island chain without firing a shot. Put Beijing's position in its own words and say what Taipei is doing in response.

stories.label: ECB Set to Hold Rates to Assess France and Energy Risks
stories.summary: The ECB decides today and is expected to hold its deposit rate at 2.5%. It faces two shocks pulling opposite ways: bond-market turmoil in France and energy costs rising again with the Iran war, after EU gas passed €100. The euro is at its weakest since May 2025 going into the meeting. Name the ECB deposit rate and the euro. Explain why a war-driven energy shock leaves a central bank unable either to cut or to hike, and who pays: indebted France and households facing the winter heating bill.

stories.label: Copper's AI-fuelled boom gets a reality check
stories.summary: The Yangshan premium, what Chinese importers pay above the LME price, jumped past $200 a ton on Wednesday, a record. Lead with that number. The mechanism: data centres, grid build-out and Chinese stockpiling are competing for metal that is 'sold out everywhere', and the premium shows where the squeeze lands first. Name the copper price, and say who pays downstream: grid builders and manufacturers in importing countries.

stories.label: Commodity prices to surge 23pc, warns World Bank
stories.summary: The World Bank expects global commodity prices to rise 23% in 2026, driven by war-driven energy costs, shipping disruption in the Middle East, Black Sea grain problems and safe-haven demand for gold. Lead with who pays: fuel- and food-importing developing economies, Pakistan among them, through fertiliser, food and import bills. Name Brent crude and gold. Dawn's Pakistani framing is the regional voice.

stories.label: New atlas of colorectal tumors sheds light on why cancers in young people are more dangerous
stories.summary: Dana-Farber researchers profiled 189 colorectal tumours from patients in their 20s to their 90s, in a study published in Nature. Lead with the biological difference they found in early-onset tumours. Then the stakes: colorectal cancer in people under 50 is rising worldwide, and screening starts too late to catch it. Explain what the finding means for screening ages and treatment.

stories.label: Analysis: China’s clean-tech exports in 2026 to avoid as much CO2 as Brazil emits in a year
stories.summary: Carbon Brief estimates that the solar panels, batteries and EVs China exports in 2026 will avoid as much CO2 over their lifetimes as Brazil emits in a year. Lead with that comparison. Then explain the method, and which buyers in the Global South (Pakistan, Africa, Southeast Asia) drive the figure. The mechanism: China's industrial overcapacity is now decarbonising other countries faster than their own climate policies.

stories.label: Senators Demand Meta Answer for 'Pervert Glasses' Following 404 Media Investigation
stories.summary: Senators Wyden and Markey have written to Meta demanding answers after a 404 Media investigation tied its smart glasses to covert filming of people who never consented. Lead with the bystander, who has no way to opt out of a camera worn as eyewear. Say what the letter demands, the deadline, and what 404 Media found. The accountability gap: no law covers wearable recording in public.

stories.label: UK MOD Awards £15 Million Orbital Warfare Project to Astroscale
stories.summary: Britain's Ministry of Defence has given Astroscale's UK arm £15m for Project LEDA, which an MoD official calls part of 'the permanent pathway for UK's understanding of orbital warfare'. The surprising detail: Astroscale built its name on cleaning up space debris, and the same docking technology for approaching satellites can disable them. Lead with that dual use and the quiet militarisation of orbit.

stories.label: Three killed by storm in southern India
stories.summary: Cyclone Arnab came ashore near Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh as a 'very severe cyclonic storm', killed at least three, then weakened into a deep depression; Andhra Pradesh and Odisha remain under rain alerts. Lead with the landfall and the toll, then who was evacuated and why India's cyclone-warning system now keeps tolls this low on a coast that once lost thousands to such storms. A disaster story, filed as politics.

stories.label: Iran keeps diplomacy open as US weighs fresh strikes
stories.summary: New development: Qatar has put a seven-day plan to end the war on the table, Araghchi says Tehran is 'in contact' with mediators while an Iranian official calls the ideas 'unacceptable', and the WSJ reports Washington has warned Gulf states of a 'short, intense' war on Iran after the 3 November midterms. Lead with the timing: a war restart scheduled around a US election, with Gulf states who host the bases told to brace. Note Brent crude above $116 as the stake.

stories.label: Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, Historic Mexican Politician and Former Presidential Candidate, Dies at 92
stories.summary: Cárdenas, announced dead by President Sheinbaum, broke from the PRI and ran in 1988 in an election widely believed stolen from him by a 'system crash' in the count. Lead with that: the man whose defeat began the end of seven decades of one-party rule, and whose left eventually won power through Morena. Son of Lázaro Cárdenas, who nationalised Mexico's oil.

stories.label: US judge handling deposed Venezuelan president Maduro's case dies
stories.summary: Judge Alvin Hellerstein, 92, who was presiding over the US prosecution of the deposed Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro in Manhattan, has died. Lead with what happens to the case now: reassignment to a new judge, likely delay, and a trial that tests whether a US court can try a head of state removed by US force. Keep it distinct from the Venezuela negotiations story covered yesterday.

stories.label: Why is Egypt jumping into Houthi war? First, follow the money.
stories.summary: Egypt's parliament, after two postponements, authorised Sisi to take 'necessary measures' to defend Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, and a Houthi figure called it a 'declaration of war'. The mechanism: about $18bn of Saudi, Kuwaiti and Qatari deposits make up nearly a third of Egypt's $57bn reserves, the pound is at a record 56 to the dollar, and debt service takes 64% of the budget. What Egypt risks is ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb and the Suez Canal, whose revenue fell from $10.2bn in 2023 to about $4bn. Attribute the analysis to the outlet; state the vote and the figures as fact only where they are public record.

stories.label: Alphabet stock sinks as search woes cause revenue miss, cash burn worsens
stories.summary: Alphabet's free cash flow turned negative (about -$9.1bn) as quarterly capex jumped 114% to $51.4bn for AI, while Google Cloud revenue doubled (+103%) and search missed; shares fell about 10% after hours. Lead with the negative cash flow: the world's most profitable ad business now spends more than it earns to build AI capacity. The quarter's results, not the Gemini 4 Carbon launch, which ran yesterday. Zhidx (Chinese tech press) has the full earnings-call breakdown, including a $561bn cloud backlog.

stories.label: Al Gharbia Pipe Company expects new demand as Middle East nations bypass Hormuz | The National
stories.summary: 'Every country in the region is considering a new pipeline to avoid Hormuz,' says the head of Abu Dhabi's Al Gharbia Pipe Company. Lead with the structural shift: eight months of war have Gulf states and Iraq planning to route oil around the Strait of Hormuz, which changes who controls the export routes and how much of the Gulf's oil passes through the strait. Name the bypass lines that already exist (Habshan–Fujairah, Saudi East-West) and what is being planned. Chart: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: DHS investigates massive data breach exposing 40,000 employees, including ICE and Border Patrol agents
stories.summary: A self-described anti-fascist hacking group claims to have leaked personnel records for about 40,000 DHS staff, including ICE and Border Patrol agents, and DHS is investigating. Lead with the scale and how the data got out (what system, what fields), then the collision of two accountability fights: masked immigration agents whose identities the public has sought, and the doxxing risk to individuals. Attribute the claim to the group and the figures to DHS; don't treat Fox's framing as fact.

stories.label: 央企名列第28：国家数据集团的起点，为什么这么高？
stories.summary: China's new National Data Group has been listed as the 100th central state-owned enterprise and ranked 28th, above established electronics makers, a ranking set by state strategy rather than size. Lead with what Beijing is building: a state operator for data as a 'factor of production', separating the regulator (the National Data Administration) from the operator, with Xiong'an as the testbed. The inside view from mainland tech press: what the business model is and where the centre and the provinces clash over data.

stories.label: Neighbours: AI micro-drama recut of Australian show focusing on Margot Robbie worries actors and crew
stories.summary: Fremantle and US-based RoseBerry Media plan to use AI to scan the old footage of Neighbours and cut new mini-episodes for phones, built around actors such as Margot Robbie who signed contracts decades before AI existed. Lead with the rights gap: performers whose old work is being remade into new product without new consent or pay. Explain what the AI does, and what Australian actors' unions say their contracts cover.

stories.label: A Ballot-Stacking Effort in Alaska
stories.summary: Democratic operatives aligned with Mary Peltola's Senate campaign spent months recruiting spoiler candidates to split the vote in Alaska's ranked-choice system; Trump now demands Peltola be prosecuted and barred from the race a week before the midterms. Lead with the mechanism — how a ballot is stacked under ranked-choice voting — and the president calling for an opponent's prosecution. Dateline Anchorage.

stories.label: SSA operation targeting EFF lacked national security basis, court told
stories.summary: The Gauteng High Court heard that South Africa's State Security Agency ran Project Mayibuye, a secret operation against the opposition EFF with no national-security basis, and channelled millions through it. Lead with a state intelligence agency spending public money to spy on a political party, a week before the 4 November local elections; name who authorised it and where the money went.

stories.label: Noreen Niazi moved from Lahore jail to hospital due to high blood pressure: lawyer
stories.summary: Three sisters of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan — Noreen Niazi, Aleema Khan and Uzma Khan — are themselves detained in Kot Lakhpat jail, and Noreen has now been moved to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology. Lead with the detention of a prisoner's family as a pressure tactic: how long they have been held, on what charges, and what the courts have done.

stories.label: After 3 months of negotiations, could Venezuela’s negotiation table be a game changer for the country?
stories.summary: The third round of government–opposition talks in post-Maduro Venezuela ended on 21 October with movement on releasing political prisoners, unblocking media outlets and a committee to nominate new Supreme Tribunal justices. Lead with what has actually been delivered — how many prisoners freed, which outlets unblocked — against what was promised, and who controls the court nominations.

stories.label: Lula vence em seções eleitorais com local alterado, apesar de abstenção maior
stories.summary: Agência Pública's analysis of Brazil's runoff: polling sections whose location was moved between the first and second round had higher abstention, yet 16 of them flipped to Lula. Lead with the data on relocated sections — who moved them, how many voters were affected — and what it says about whether relocation suppressed turnout. A data story, distinct from earlier coverage of Lula's online campaign.

stories.label: Nigeria renews 2030 gas flaring pledge despite enforcement, methane monitoring gaps
stories.summary: Nigeria's upstream regulator renewed its pledge to end routine gas flaring by 2030 — a deadline already missed several times — while Premium Times investigations document constant flaring at oil facilities, weak enforcement and no independent methane verification. Lead with the gap between pledge and practice: the gas burned and the revenue lost, the Niger Delta communities breathing it, and the operators (TotalEnergies among them) who pay fines cheaper than capture.

stories.label: Tokayev Proposes Dipping Into National Fund to Turn Kazakhstan into a ‘Big Construction Site’
stories.summary: In his state of the nation address, President Tokayev proposed drawing on Kazakhstan's oil-savings National Fund to finance an infrastructure and investment spree. Lead with the trade-off: a sovereign fund built to outlast the oil is being spent now — how much, on what, and what that means for the tenge and for the next generation's buffer.

stories.label: Bitcoin-backed mortgages are coming to Canada, but borrowers are still unaware of the cost
stories.summary: Canadian lender APX Lending will offer bitcoin-backed mortgages from early 2027, letting buyers pledge bitcoin instead of selling it for a down payment. Name the series: bitcoin. Lead with the mechanism and the risk — what happens to the collateral, and the home, when bitcoin falls through the liquidation threshold — and who regulates it.

stories.label: Explaining the difference between brittle and ductile behavior in polymer glasses
stories.summary: Researchers explain why glassy polymers like PMMA (acrylic glass) shatter in some conditions and stretch in others, depending on chemistry, temperature and deformation rate. Lead with the finding — what decides whether a plastic snaps or yields — and why it matters for designing tougher transparent materials.

stories.label: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its latest frontier AI model that you can't use
stories.summary: Two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon, Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon — a frontier model the public cannot use. Lead with the access gap: who gets it, why Google is withholding it (safety, compute, or competition), and what the release cadence says about the frontier-lab race.

stories.label: If You're In the UK or EU, Here's How to Object to Meta's AI Training
stories.summary: Meta's new terms let it scrape users' posts and data to train AI; only users in the EU and UK, under GDPR, can object — and only for now. Lead with the asymmetry: billions of users elsewhere have no opt-out at all. Explain what the terms cover and how the objection works. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: China’s CE-25A Electric Commuter Airliner Demonstrator Emerges
stories.summary: Photos show China's CE-25A, a 19-seat electric commuter airliner demonstrator with an unusual array of ducted fans. Lead with the engineering — distributed electric propulsion at commuter scale — and its dual-use implications beyond civil aviation, as China pushes ahead of Western electric-aviation programmes.

stories.label: Trump admin sues Utah to save Kalshi from the state's total ban on gambling
stories.summary: The CFTC sued Utah — the tenth state it has sued — to stop it enforcing its total gambling ban against prediction-market platform Kalshi. Lead with the federal regulator acting as the industry's lawyer against states' power to ban gambling, and the mechanism: classifying bets as federally regulated 'event contracts' to pre-empt state law. Dateline Salt Lake City.

stories.label: Iranians face energy squeeze from war as natural gas runs short
stories.summary: US and Israeli strikes damaged Iran's gas-processing plants, and Tehran is now telling citizens to cut use of heavily subsidised natural gas and civil servants to work from home before winter. Lead with who pays: ordinary households in a country with some of the world's largest gas reserves, facing a heating shortage because the processing, not the gas, was bombed. Name the series: natural gas. Datelined Tehran.

stories.label: US Wins Over 23 More Countries in UN Vote Against Cuba Embargo
stories.summary: 130 states again condemned the US embargo on Cuba (34th year), but 17 voted against and 25 abstained — 23 more than last year — after a US campaign of threatened tariffs, visa denials and aid cuts. Lead with who flipped (UAE, Lithuania, Slovenia, Costa Rica, Colombia, Honduras, Chile) and the mechanism of the arm-twisting; then what the embargo does on the island now — the 30% tariff threat on fuel shippers that has deepened Cuba's blackouts and hit hospitals, water and food distribution. Datelined Havana.

stories.label: One hour to leave: Hebron families displaced by Israel’s military operation don’t know when they’ll return
stories.summary: Israeli forces have expelled 407 Palestinian families — nearly 2,650 people — from their homes in Hebron, given one hour and one bag, sealed the city's entrances and closed the Ibrahimi Mosque to Muslim worshippers. Lead with the numbers and the closure of the mosque; name the unit and authority ordering it, and the absence of any return date. Continuation of displacement is the development. Datelined Hebron.

stories.label: Ethiopia Gets 12 Russian Su-35 Fighters, Eyes S-400 Air Defenses
stories.summary: Abiy Ahmed says 12 Russian Su-35 fighters arrived a year early and four S-400 batteries are to follow — making Ethiopia one of the few African air forces with front-line Russian jets. Lead with the deal's size; the stakes are Ethiopia's tensions with Eritrea and Egypt over the Red Sea and the Nile dam, and Russia's widening arms and port reach on Africa's east coast. Datelined Addis Ababa.

stories.label: Um ano após chacina, as crianças da Penha precisam voltar a ser crianças
stories.summary: A year after the Rio police raid on the Penha and Alemão favelas — the deadliest police operation in Brazil's history — the politicians who backed it have just been elected, while children in the communities still live with the trauma. Lead with that contrast: accountability that never came, rewarded at the ballot box. Give the raid's death toll and what investigations found. Datelined Rio de Janeiro.

stories.label: Fed likely to go into wait-and-see mode on rates
stories.summary: The Fed held its rate at 3.75-4% under Chair Kevin Warsh, a month after its first hike in three years, saying more data will guide the next move — the last decision before the US midterms, fought over the cost of living and oil-driven inflation from the Iran war. Lead with the decision and any dissents; name the series: the Fed funds rate, the US 10-year Treasury yield, US inflation. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: Is This What Being "In Hock" Looks Like?: The Readout
stories.summary: Material new development beyond this morning's gas standing-charge story: Chancellor John Healey has now delivered Burnham's first budget, and its frame is the fiscal damage of the Iran war — higher energy costs, weaker growth and borrowing per the OBR. Lead with the headline borrowing and tax numbers and who pays; the mechanism is how a war 5,000km away blew a hole in Britain's public finances. Do not re-lead on standing charges. Datelined London.

stories.label: Why the world's first spinal cord transplant is so controversial | New Scientist
stories.summary: Surgeons in Russia have performed the first spinal cord transplant in people, but the animal and clinical evidence behind it is thin. Lead with what was done and on whom; the mechanism is why spinal tissue rarely reconnects, and the accountability question is consent and evidence standards when a first-in-human operation outruns the data. Datelined Moscow.

stories.label: How Spiders Spin ‘Silk Dope’ Into Nature’s Toughest Material
stories.summary: Biologists probing the molecular structure of spider 'silk dope' are finding how a tangle of unstructured proteins, held as liquid condensates, turns into a thread tougher than steel by weight. Lead with that transformation; the stakes are why decades of synthetic-silk attempts failed and what the mechanism means for materials.

stories.label: Evidence of a spying operation by ICE against left-wing social movements
stories.summary: Wired reports ICE is running one of the largest surveillance operations against left-wing movements in US history — a 'Cointelpro 2.0'. Lead with the scale and the tools (social-media monitoring, data brokers, informants) and who is targeted; the accountability gap is an immigration agency turned domestic political police days before the midterms. 982 points on Hacker News signals reader attention. Datelined Washington.

stories.label: US sanctions Russians, North Koreans for laundering IT worker earnings
stories.summary: The US Treasury sanctioned Russian and North Korean nationals for laundering the pay of North Korean remote IT workers who pose as freelancers at foreign tech firms. Lead with the laundering route through Russia; the mechanism is how hidden remote hires fund Pyongyang's weapons programme, and the Russia–North Korea financial channel the war has deepened. Datelined Pyongyang.

stories.label: Anthropic巨亏背后，藏着行业什么秘密？
stories.summary: TMTPost reads Anthropic's heavy losses as a structural fact of the AI industry: model companies' valuations are parasitic on their infrastructure suppliers — the cloud and chip firms that invest in them and take the money back as compute spend. Lead with the loss figures and the circular-financing mechanism; this is how China's tech press reads the US AI boom. Datelined Beijing.

stories.label: Präsidentschaftswahl in Brasilien: Gewonnen mit und trotz Internet
stories.summary: Lula won re-election despite a Brazilian right that dominates social media, with an online operation led by André Janones that used the networks to drive mobilisation on the ground rather than to win the feed. Lead with that mechanism — how a left campaign beat platform asymmetry — and what it says about elections run on WhatsApp and YouTube. Datelined Brasília.

stories.label: At least 10 dead after two trains collide in Spain
stories.summary: Two high-speed trains collided head-on near Urda, Toledo, killing at least 10, and officials expect the toll to rise. Lead with the toll and the question the reports raise: how two trains on Spain's high-speed network, run by Renfe and Iryo, ended up on the same track, and whether a rail fracture was the cause. Datelined Toledo.

stories.label: 4 Takeaways From Israel's Election
stories.summary: The results are in and neither Netanyahu's bloc (about 53 seats with 85.6% counted, per Middle East Eye) nor Eisenkot's opposition reaches a Knesset majority without the Palestinian parties. Lead with that arithmetic: the only path to a non-Netanyahu government runs through the parties of Israel's Palestinian citizens, whose turnout was historic (New Lines). The structural why: both blocs treat an Arab partner as taboo, so the choice is breaking it or a sixth election in under a decade. Datelined Jerusalem.

stories.label: Oil prices up due to Houthi strikes and US threat to renew Iran war | The National
stories.summary: A Houthi attack on a Saudi Arabian refinery and Washington's threat to resume the war on Iran pushed Brent crude back up, past $116 for the second time in October (Mehr), and UBS now expects Brent near $110 through year-end on falling inventories and record freight costs. Lead with the refinery strike as the cause; the mechanism is supply already squeezed by Hormuz, so each new attack moves the price. Name the series: Brent crude and WTI crude. Datelined where the refinery was hit.

stories.label: John Healey to end standing charges on gas bills for 23m homes
stories.summary: Ahead of his first budget, Chancellor John Healey will ask Ofgem to abolish the fixed daily standing charge on gas bills for 23 million homes from 2027, saving about £45 a year on average. Lead with the mechanism: the standing charge is paid regardless of use, so it falls hardest on low-use, low-income households, and removing it shifts network costs onto the per-unit price. Name the series: natural gas. Datelined London.

stories.label: Adani returns to profit on copper, renewables and airports units
stories.summary: Adani Enterprises broke its streak of quarterly losses in July-September, carried by its copper smelter, renewable-equipment and airports units. Lead with copper: the Kutch smelter turned a profit as copper prices ran high, which shows where India's largest infrastructure conglomerate now makes its money. Name the series: copper. TimesNow carries the full Q2 figures. Datelined Ahmedabad.

stories.label: Highwaymen: How Cargo Theft Gangs Operate in Costa Rica
stories.summary: Gangs hijacking trucks on Costa Rica's highways use leaked customs data to pick their loads and signal jammers to kill trackers. InSight Crime rode with a Panamanian trucker along the Central American corridor. Lead with the customs-data leak: the theft starts inside the state's own system, which makes it a corruption story as much as a crime story. Datelined San José.

stories.label: Russia plans to establish transport hub on Africa's east coast -- Deputy Foreign Minister
stories.summary: At the Russia-Africa economic forum, Deputy Foreign Minister Sergey Ryabkov said Moscow plans a port and logistics hub on Africa's east coast as part of the International North-South Transport Corridor, and PhosAgro said it will double fertiliser shipments to Africa this year (South Africa, Ethiopia and Mozambique the top buyers). Lead with the hub: it extends a corridor built to route Russian trade around Western sanctions and Suez. Both claims come via Russian state agency TASS and must be attributed. Datelined Moscow.

stories.label: Antarctic sea-ice loss could reshape weather far beyond the pole
stories.summary: A paper published Wednesday documents a sharp rise in salinity in Antarctic surface waters since sea ice began its rapid decline in 2016. Lead with the mechanism: saltier surface water mixes more easily with the warm deep layer, which melts more ice from below, and that feedback can shift ocean circulation and weather far from the pole. Datelined at the research institution.

stories.label: A 60-year search is over: Chemists isolate long-elusive molecules with boron-oxygen triple bonds
stories.summary: Chemists at the University of Würzburg, with computations from Tezpur University in India, report in Nature Chemistry a way to make and isolate stable oxoboranes, molecules with a boron-oxygen triple bond that chemists have chased for over 60 years. Lead with why they were thought too reactive to keep, and what a stable one opens for boron chemistry. Datelined Würzburg.

stories.label: EU-Kommission: Frontex soll zur Abschiebeagentur werden
stories.summary: Two draft laws from the European Commission would turn the border agency Frontex into the EU's central deportation agency, with more staff, more powers and social-media monitoring among its tools; an MEP warns it could become a European version of US immigration police ICE. Lead with the surveillance: what data Frontex would collect on migrants and who checks it. Datelined Brussels.

stories.label: 下中国象棋赢了Jev！扩散智能推出决策模型，判断正确率达95%
stories.summary: Shenzhen startup DiffuSpace, founded by HKU NLP researcher Kong Lingpeng, open-sourced Clover-35B-A3B, a diffusion language model (35B total, 3B active parameters) that it says beats the same-size autoregressive Qwen on six agent and coding benchmarks (SWE-bench Verified 73.6) and generates 680 tokens/s on one GB300. Lead with the architecture bet: diffusion models write blocks of text in parallel instead of one token at a time. Benchmarks are the company's own; say so. Datelined Shenzhen.

stories.label: FBI seizes ‘bulletproof’ hosting site accused of facilitating child abuse, money laundering
stories.summary: The FBI seized the domain of Virtualine, a 'bulletproof' hosting provider accused of hosting child sexual abuse material and serving money launderers and other cybercriminals. Lead with the business model: bulletproof hosts sell immunity from takedown requests, and seizing one knocks out every criminal operation on it at once. Datelined Washington.
